title: Unexpected resident arenas during rolling batch migration
creator: Priya Nair
body: Summary: After enabling the rolling-batch migration (continuous batching + KV prefetch) in the development cluster, we observe a steady increase in resident GPU arenas over long tails of mixed small/large requests. Memory never returns to baseline between bursts, causing OOMs on high-concurrency stages. This ticket tracks the root-cause analysis and proposed mitigations for allocator behavior (cudaMallocAsync + pooling) and KV prefetch interactions.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.19 with rolling-batch-migration flag enabled on 4x A100 nodes.

2) Run the mixed-batch workload (script: scripts/repro/rolling_batch_migration.sh) that alternates small chat messages (<=64 tokens, high QPS) and large context warmups (~4096 tokens) with KV prefetch enabled (prefetch_window=300).
3) Observe pod metrics: gpu_resident_arenas increases by ~20% over 6 hours and does not drop between bursts.
4) Collect nvml snapshots, cudaMemPool reports and periodic GPU process maps for heap analysis.
5) Re-run with allocator debug logging enabled (ENV: ALLOC_DEBUG=1) and sample every minute.
Note: repro script attached to attachments; reproducible in ~4-6 hours in our staging environment.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-26 - Initial triage by Priya: memory trend started after enabling an optimization that prefetches KV for anticipated next-request sequences. No immediate increase in cudaMallocAsync failure rates but overall resident arena count rises.

2026-03-01 - Lukas: Collected cudaMemPool logs using cudaMemPoolGetAttribute and sampled GPU snapshots. Observed large slab buckets marked as resident and not returned to pool between large->small batch transitions.

2026-03-03 - Perf instrumentation: allocation peak corresponds to large-context minibatch, but free ops are being recorded on a different stream; cudaFreeAsync is enqueued but cudaMemPoolTrim not invoked due to pool hysteresis thresholds.

2026-03-05 - Heap walk (host-side) shows fragmentation: many mid-size allocations (~256KB-2MB) persist as free fragments inside arenas that are prevented from coalescing because the allocator's deferred free queue holds them for cross-stream synchronization.

2026-03-07 - KV cache interaction: prefetch writes increase transient allocations and populate hot slices. When prefetch window shrinks, eviction triggers but eviction path uses cudaFreeAsync on separate streams that are not synchronizing with the pool's coalesce path, leaving arenas partially full.

2026-03-09 - Hypothesis: combination of (A) deferred frees across streams, (B) pool hysteresis (to avoid churn) and (C) KV prefetch pattern causes persistent fragmentation and prevents arena trimming. The allocator favors resident arenas because trimming threshold (trim_after_ms) is too large for our mixed-batch workload.
nvml snapshot notes: reserved memory snapshots match resident arena growth; no leaks at process level (total device reserved aligned with expected peak) but arenas remain pinned due to pool behavior.
Related artifacts: dashboard (Grafana) showing gpu_arena_resident_count, cudaMallocAsync latency, and kv_prefetch_eviction_rate attached.
proposed_fixes: Short-term mitigation (fast roll): reduce prefetch_window to 80 and lower pool hysteresis: set ALLOC_POOL_TRIM_MS=15000 and ALLOC_POOL_HYSTERESIS_RATIO=0.25 to force earlier trimming in staging.

Medium-term change: implement stream-aware deferred-free drain: when epoch boundary is detected (end of request batch), synchronously drain deferred-free queue for arenas that cross a fragmentation watermark.

Long-term: enhance pooling logic to prefer cross-arena coalescing: add an arena compaction pass that attempts to move small live allocations onto consolidated arenas before returning empty arenas to OS/pool-trim.
Add metrics and tracing points: deferred_free_queue_depth, arena_fragmentation_ratio, last_trim_timestamp to help operationally detect regressions.
Fallback policy: when resident_arenas > X and eviction_rate < Y, automatically disable prefetch for the tenant and fallback to on-demand KV loads.
